paragraphs.text: LCHAD deficiency is a defect of fatty acid breakdown. It is associated with life-threatening episodes of hypoketotic hypoglycemia during prolonged fasting, and neuropathy and retinal pigment changes have also been noted (Schrijver-Wieling et al., 1997). LCHAD catalyzes the third step of mitochondrial beta-oxidation, and its activity sits on the C-terminal portion of the alpha subunit of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein (Sims et al., 1995). The trifunctional protein also carries long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase and long-chain 3-ketothiolase activities (IJlst et al., 1994).

paragraphs.text: den Boer et al. (2002) reviewed questionnaire data on 50 of 61 unselected patients with LCHAD deficiency diagnosed at their center. The mean age at clinical presentation was 5.8 months (range, 1 day to 26 months), and 7 patients (15%) presented in the neonatal period. Thirty-nine patients (78%) presented with hypoketotic hypoglycemia. The other 11 (22%) presented with chronic problems consisting of failure to thrive, feeding difficulties, cholestatic liver disease, and/or hypotonia. In retrospect, 82% of the patients who presented with an acute metabolic derangement had also had a combination of chronic nonspecific symptoms before the metabolic crises. paragraphs.text: Jones et al. (2003) used an in vitro model to study the effects of dietary treatment in LCHAD deficiency. They grew cultured skin fibroblasts from LCHAD-deficient and normal individuals in media supplemented with physiologic combinations of the medium-chain fatty acids octanoate and decanoate and the long-chain fatty acid palmitate. Adding medium-chain fatty acids decreased the accumulation of long-chain fatty acid oxidation intermediates in LCHAD-deficient cells, both in untreated medium and with added palmitate, and decanoate alone was more effective than octanoate alone. Over an extended time, a 1:3 ratio of octanoate to decanoate worked best in untreated medium, whereas a 1:1 ratio worked best in medium containing palmitate. checks.evidence_quote: While carrying fetuses with the Glu474Gln mutation, 79 percent of the heterozygous mothers had fatty liver of pregnancy or the HELLP syndrome.

paragraphs.text: In a separate report, Ibdah et al. (1999) found homozygosity for the 1528G-C (E474Q) mutation in an infant with LCHAD deficiency who presented with hypocalcemia and cholestatic liver disease and died suddenly at 8 months.

checks.claim: Ibdah et al. (1999) found homozygosity for the HADHA 1528G-C (E474Q) mutation in an infant with LCHAD deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Molecular analysis revealed homozygosity for the prevalent LCHAD (1528G > C, E474Q) mutation.
checks.explanation: The abstract says 'LCHAD' rather than HADHA. Using the gene symbol is a standard nomenclature restatement.

checks.claim: The infant with LCHAD deficiency homozygous for HADHA E474Q presented with hypocalcemia.
checks.evidence_quote: The proband presented at 2 months of age with an acute infantile hypocalcaemia

checks.claim: The infant with LCHAD deficiency homozygous for HADHA E474Q presented with cholestatic liver disease.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with occult, unexplained cholestatic liver disease.

checks.claim: The infant with LCHAD deficiency homozygous for HADHA E474Q died suddenly at 8 months of age.
checks.evidence_quote: Sudden, unexpected death occurred at 8 months.

paragraphs.text: Baskin et al. (2010) found a child with LCHAD deficiency who was homozygous for the c.1526G-C (p.Glu510Gln) mutation. The father was heterozygous and the mother did not carry it. Short tandem repeat analysis showed that the homozygosity resulted from paternal uniparental isodisomy of chromosome 2.

checks.claim: Baskin et al. (2010) found a child with LCHAD deficiency who was homozygous for the HADHA c.1526G-C (p.Glu510Gln) mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: the child was homozygous for the common mutation, c.1526G > C (p.Glu510Gln) in the HADHA gene
checks.explanation: Same variant written in equivalent notation.

checks.claim: The father of the child reported by Baskin et al. (2010) was heterozygous for the HADHA p.Glu510Gln mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: the father was heterozygous for the mutation whereas the mother did not carry the mutation

checks.claim: The mother of the child reported by Baskin et al. (2010) did not carry the HADHA p.Glu510Gln mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: the father was heterozygous for the mutation whereas the mother did not carry the mutation

checks.claim: Short tandem repeat analysis showed that the child's homozygosity for HADHA p.Glu510Gln resulted from paternal uniparental isodisomy of chromosome 2.
checks.evidence_quote: Short tandem repeat testing with markers covering both short and long arms of chromosome 2 showed that the child has paternal uniparental isodisomy.

paragraphs.text: Elizondo et al. (2020) found that 9 of 11 patients with LCHAD/TFP deficiency were homozygous or compound heterozygous for c.1528G-C (E510Q). These carriers had consistently higher C16-OH, C18-OH, and C18:1-OH levels than the 2 patients without the variant.

checks.claim: Elizondo et al. (2020) found that 9 of 11 patients with LCHAD/TFP deficiency were homozygous or compound heterozygous for HADHA c.1528G-C (E510Q).
checks.evidence_quote: Nine of these eleven participants were either homozygous or compound heterozygous for the common pathogenic HADHA variant c.1528G>C.

checks.claim: LCHAD/TFP-deficient patients carrying HADHA c.1528G-C had consistently higher C16-OH, C18-OH, and C18:1-OH levels than the 2 patients without the variant.
checks.evidence_quote: All patients with the common mutation (c.1528G>C) in at least one HADHA allele had consistently higher levels of C16-OH, C18-OH and C18:1-OH than the two patients without the common pathogenic variant

paragraphs.text: In a child with LCHAD deficiency whose mother had acute fatty liver of pregnancy, Sims et al. (1995) found compound heterozygosity for 2 mutations in the HADHA gene. One was a C-to-T transition at nucleotide 1132 (C1132T), which creates a premature stop codon at residue 342. The other was the common G1528C (E474Q) mutation.

checks.claim: Sims et al. (1995) found compound heterozygosity for 2 HADHA mutations in a child with LCHAD deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: The third child had this G1528C mutation on one allele and a different mutation (C1132T) creating a premature termination codon (residue 342) on the second allele.

checks.claim: The mother of the compound heterozygous LCHAD-deficient child reported by Sims et al. (1995) had acute fatty liver of pregnancy.
checks.evidence_quote: In all families, the mothers had acute fatty liver and associated sever complications during pregnancies with the affected infants.
checks.explanation: This applies to all families, including the compound heterozygous child's family.

checks.claim: One HADHA mutation in the compound heterozygous child was a C-to-T transition at nucleotide 1132 (C1132T).
checks.evidence_quote: a different mutation (C1132T) creating a premature termination codon (residue 342) on the second allele
checks.explanation: C1132T is a C-to-T transition at nucleotide 1132.

checks.claim: The HADHA C1132T mutation creates a premature stop codon at residue 342.
checks.evidence_quote: a different mutation (C1132T) creating a premature termination codon (residue 342)

checks.claim: The other HADHA mutation in the compound heterozygous child was the common G1528C (E474Q) mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: The third child had this G1528C mutation on one allele
checks.explanation: The child carried G1528C (E474Q), but the abstract does not call this mutation 'common'. That label is not in the paper.
